items.defectStatement: getClientsWithPermission searches for type "Clients", which matches the all-clients resource but misses untyped per-client resources. It consequently returns an empty set or the literal "Clients" instead of internal client IDs, causing missing role mappings or a null dereference in its caller.
obligations: Return internal client IDs for clients granted the requested scope.
Include grants on untyped per-client resources and applicable all-clients grants.
Preserve client-specific resource precedence and the existing realm/resource-server guards.
Do not return resource-type names or dereference missing resources.
items.notes: The frozen input omits the inherited realm field and client-enumeration API. getClientId() is the wrong identifier: the caller uses getClientById(). Merely assigning types elsewhere would not expand an all-clients grant into actual client IDs.

items.defectStatement: canView(client) accepts an all-clients VIEW grant before evaluating the client's explicit resource, bypassing a client-specific denial. ClientsResource.getClients also independently uses canView() to skip per-client authorization.
obligations: Evaluate client-specific permissions before applying the all-clients fallback.
Ensure listing cannot bypass client-specific denials through its global shortcut.
Preserve built-in administrative role access and legitimate configure/manage grants.
Preserve listing eligibility and correct pagination when filtering individual clients.
items.notes: Replacing canView() with canViewClientDefault() at this anchor fixes the direct check only. The listing shortcut remains outside the anchor; its implementation and inherited listing checks are absent from the frozen input.

items.defectStatement: The V1-only feature guard skips removal handling in V2-only configurations, leaving V2 per-client authorization resources behind. If the guarded listener runs while management() selects V2, client deletion instead calls setPermissionsEnabled(), which throws UnsupportedOperationException.
obligations: Clean up a deleted client's V2 authorization resource without calling the unsupported V2 setter.
Preserve legacy client, role, and group cleanup.
Preserve permissions for surviving resources when removing shared policy associations.
Handle absent authorization resources and unrelated events without failure.
items.notes: Inline cleanup fits the anchor; adding a cleanup API elsewhere is optional. The frozen input lacks V2 naming and store-deletion behavior. The repository's wrapped resource store cleans policy associations on deletion. V2's schema defines Users and Clients, so the finding overstates V2-specific role/group resources.

items.defectStatement: When neither the client-specific resource nor the all-clients resource exists, hasPermission(client, scope) passes null to findByResource. This causes a null dereference instead of denying permission.
obligations: Return false when the fallback resource is absent.
Do not query policies or evaluate permissions with a null resource.
Preserve evaluation of existing resources and denial when the fallback has no policies.
items.notes: The outer closing brace is outside the anchor and must remain there. A separate null guard is equally valid.

items.defectStatement: canView() ignores an all-clients MANAGE grant, even though manage permits viewing individual clients. Without a query role, inherited canList() rejects listing; with a query role, listing unnecessarily fetches unpaginated candidates and evaluates each client.
obligations: Recognize an all-clients MANAGE grant as granting global view eligibility.
Preserve existing default-role and all-clients VIEW grants.
Do not treat a grant limited to one client as a global grant.
items.notes: Calling canManage() is also valid. This fixes the missing MANAGE implication independently; the global listing shortcut's handling of client-specific denials remains the separate issue in #10.

items.defectStatement: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) evaluates the all-clients resource only when no per-client resource exists. An existing per-client resource that does not grant the requested scope therefore masks a valid all-clients grant.
obligations: Accept a per-client grant for the requested scope.
Accept an all-clients grant even when a per-client resource exists without a matching grant.
Deny when neither resource grants the requested scope, including when resources are absent.
Preserve the existing same-realm and resource-server checks.
items.notes: The existing evaluation below the anchor evaluates the all-clients resource after the replacement. The helper hasGrantedPermission is fully shown in the frozen diff; no wider change is needed.

items.defectStatement: The negative removal test catches ForbiddenException from the restricted getDefaultClientScopes() call before removeDefaultClientScope() executes. Consequently, this assertion passes even when unauthorized removal is allowed.
obligations: Obtain an existing default scope ID through the privileged client outside the exception assertion.
Invoke removal through the restricted client before granting permissions.
Fail if removal succeeds or throws anything other than ForbiddenException.
Preserve the subsequent authorized removal test.
items.notes: The closing catch brace on line 153 remains outside the replacement. Avoid declaring clientScopeRep at method scope because that name is declared later.

items.defectStatement: ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException when the client-to-client token-exchange path requests a permission decision. With FGAP V2 active, requests reaching this check fail with a server error instead of the caller's normal access-denied response.
obligations: Return a boolean permission decision instead of throwing UnsupportedOperationException.
Deny unsupported V2 exchanges rather than granting them without authorization.
Preserve the method signature used by token-exchange callers.
items.notes: Returning false is a sufficient fail-closed fix; implementing V2 token-exchange policies is unnecessary. The failure affects exchanges reaching this check, not every token-exchange request.
